author: empire state today
title: David Freund discusses leadership lessons from positive reinforcement and patience
text:
David Freund said on May 13 that starting coaching sessions by asking clients about what is going well helps open minds and encourages creativity. Freund explained that focusing on the positive at the beginning of a conversation makes people more willing to engage, while starting with problems can make them defensive.
Freund shared an example from a recent client who mentioned his dog Maxy as something going well in his life. The client highlighted the importance of patience and positive reinforcement in training Maxy, which resonated with Freund as a leadership principle. “The importance of patience and positive reinforcement,” the client said, which Freund connected to effective leadership.
Reflecting on his own experience, Freund admitted there were times when he lacked both patience and clear expectations as a leader. He described how this led to disappointment for himself and frustration among team members. “Not everyone learns the same way — and not everyone learns at the same pace,” Freund said.
Freund also discussed his personal learning challenges in school, explaining that he needed different approaches than others to succeed. He compared this understanding to using positive reinforcement when potty training children, suggesting leaders should focus on catching people doing things right rather than looking for mistakes.
He cited research showing that happy workers are more productive: “According to a study from the University of Oxford, happy workers are13% more productive than unhappy workers.” Freund concluded by encouraging leaders to practice patience and encouragement as effective strategies for improving productivity.
